overview: Mithyatva in Jainism refers to the concept of false belief or delusion, which is considered a significant impediment to spiritual progress. It is the opposite of Samyaktva (right belief) and is characterized by a misunderstanding or ignorance of the true nature of reality, leading to wrong views and actions. Mithyatva prevents the soul from attaining liberation (moksha) by binding it to the cycle of birth and death (samsara). It is categorized into five types according to traditional Jain texts: Ekantika (one-sidedness), Viparita (opposite), Vinaya (respect for wrong beliefs), Samsaya (doubt), and Ajnana (ignorance). Overcoming Mithyatva requires cultivating right belief through self-study, reflection, and guidance from enlightened beings.

primary_sources.title: Tattvartha Sutra
primary_sources.author: Umasvati
primary_sources.translation: Delusion is the cause of bondage in the cycle of birth and death.
primary_sources.notes: This aphorism highlights the fundamental role of Mithyatva in perpetuating the cycle of samsara.

misconceptions.myth: Mithyatva can be eradicated through rituals alone.
misconceptions.reality: While rituals can support spiritual practice, overcoming Mithyatva fundamentally requires inner transformation through right knowledge, faith, and conduct.
